new_critical: production-guide/H003 (checks_modify) and the three K5_Q1 checks added for the enamel-pin, sticker and woven-label pages (checks_add[28], [33], [38]) conflict with the brief pin in sentence_edits[3]. Each K5_Q1 check says "the largest text set on the page, outside the reproduced X.svg, names its medium". The same repair made the wordmark mandatory: "The guide carries the Static Union wordmark, set to the brand type system", with checks_add[48] and [49] now unconditional. The guide has exactly 4 pages and one artwork per page (checks_add[23]), so the wordmark has to sit on one of the artwork pages. The type system sets the wordmark as step 01 Display / H1 at 42 pt (its sample is STATIC UNION) and section heads as step 02 at 30 pt. Failure case: page 1 opens with the STATIC UNION wordmark at 42 pt with the Bone bar, and EMBROIDERED PATCH follows as a 30 pt section head. That page passes the brief, checks_add[45] to [49] and H004, but fails H003 because the largest text is the wordmark, not the medium. This check was on one page before, and the wordmark was optional, so the conflict is new. Fix: in all four K5_Q1 checks, exclude the wordmark as well ("outside the reproduced X.svg and the STATIC UNION wordmark"), or make them test the largest heading. Do not force a wordmark size into the brief.

checks_add on season-card-r010, r011, r012 and r013 (builders/LAYOUT-08.py line 364) say: "The crunchy local contrast and the dark halo where the pool edge meets the sky in aubine_02.jpg are visibly reduced". That feature is not in the frame. The wording was copied from the asset_plan generation prompt (the builder asserts on PLAN["aubine_02.jpg"]["prompt"]). The image was never checked. I looked at aubine_02.jpg at full resolution. Its infinity edge runs from the lower left to the cove, and it meets the turquoise cove water and the rocks, never the sky. The horizon sits well above the pool. aubine_02's defect_engineered text says only "dyed water ... plus baked contrast". A grader has no pool-and-sky edge to judge, so these 4 K2_Q2 checks get inconsistent answers. That is the asset-precision problem from feedback item 5. Fix: name only what the frame shows, for example "The crunchy local contrast and oversaturation baked into aubine_02.jpg (sky, sea and rocks) are visibly reduced on <card>, not kept or strengthened." Or name a halo only after confirming it is visible in the pixels (for example around the rocks against the sea).

checks_add[74] (sell-sheet-r004, K1_Q5), [162] (launch-post-workflow), [186] (launch-post-team), [211] (launch-post-reporting), also [4] and [38] (sell-sheet-r002/r003), plus checks_modify pitch-deck/H001 (K1_Q3). These uncleared-claim checks fail anything outside the captures that is "absent from nimbadesk_copy.txt and nimbadesk_metrics.csv". The repaired brief now says the measurement line gives the window "as our supplied files state it", and sell-sheet-r004/H001, deck add[129] and the post window checks add[164], [188] and [213] all pass "Last 30 Days" for CSAT 94%, which comes from nimbadesk_ui_09.png. That window is in neither of the two files these checks allow. So an executor that follows the pin and prints Last 30 Days under 94% passes the window check but fails a K1_Q5 check that calls the output unusable, and fails deck H001 too. brief_insertions[1] then makes every deck page and post that shows CSAT repeat that window, so the same conflict spreads to them. The other-measured-result checks (add[18], [54], [90]) accept Last 30 Days on any sheet, so r002 and r003 are exposed as well. Fix: in content_uncleared (builders/LAYOUT-09.py line 556) and pitch-deck/H001, allow that one window and add nimbadesk_ui_09.png to reference_assets. For example: "No claim, figure or product feature set on <deliverable>, outside the captures, is absent from nimbadesk_copy.txt and nimbadesk_metrics.csv, except the CSAT window Last 30 Days from nimbadesk_ui_09.png." (35 words for r004.) Add the same exception to the evidence line.

Stale duplicate cover checks survive --go and contradict the pinned brief. VERIFIERS.json has two copies each of MOTION-12/release-cover/H001 and H002. checks_modify reaches only the last copy of each, so the FIRST copies still ship: H001 "The artist name on “NIGHTFORM / Music release cover” (release-cover.png) matches the approved artist name in nightform_formats.csv exactly." (nightform_formats.csv has no artist column, and the pinned brief now sends the artist name to nightform_captions.txt), and H002 "The track name on “NIGHTFORM / Music release cover” (release-cover.png) matches the approved track name in nightform_formats.csv exactly." (the patch's own edit-13 note says “exactly” would fail LOW BEAM, which the brief now requires). I ran build_checks in memory: the cover still carries duplicate H001 and H002 ids, with both stale texts. The change_log says these copies “cannot be reached through the patch schema”. That is out of date: apply_feedback.py (modified 12:26:15, three minutes after the patch at 12:23:16) now supports checks_retire, and the MOTION-09, MOTION-10 and MOTION-13 patches use it. FIX: add checks_retire entries [{check_id: MOTION-12/release-cover/H001, occurrence: 1, check: <exact first-copy text above>, why: ...}, {check_id: MOTION-12/release-cover/H002, occurrence: 1, check: <exact first-copy text above>, why: ...}], and rewrite the “Duplicate ids, OPEN for the orchestrator” change_log line to say they are retired. I tested this in memory without writing anything: validate() returned [], retire_guard() returned {}, and no duplicate human ids remained.

Old corpus drift, not caused by this patch, and the patch schema cannot reach it. It is still a brief ambiguity of the kind feedback 1 describes. tasks/MOTION-12/OUTPUT_REGISTER.json and DELIVERABLES.md give durations of 20 to 30 s for the teaser and 12 to 15 s for the vertical. The brief (“twelve to fifteen”, “eight to ten”), TASK_SPEC, OUTPUT_REGISTER_ALL100.json and the automatic checks release-teaser/A005 (12 to 15 s) and release-vertical/A005 (8 to 10 s) all say otherwise. The brief tells the executor to trust the register, so an executor that follows it fails A005. This needs a tool-side or orchestrator fix to the per-task register and DELIVERABLES.md before --go.

not_fixed.problem: Finding 1, part 2: 'If the orchestrator holds to GUIDE rule 2 (leave existing bindings alone), escalate.'
not_fixed.why: This is an escalation, not a defect. The patch clears all eight bindings as the reviewer asked, and apply_feedback.py --only PHOTO-01 accepts it: 'accepted: 1', 8 bindings. The departure from rule 2 and its reason are recorded in change_log with a fallback: drop deliverable_bindings and reword record_field_policy instead. Leaving the bindings would keep aurelian_launch_shoot_06.jpg, the sheet prices and '(30ml frosted)' as the stated 'scoring target' in OUTPUT_REGISTER.json, and the corrected trap checks fail that. The orchestrator should confirm it accepts this deviation.

not_fixed.problem: Finding 3 and finding 13 wording differs from the reviewers' literal text.
not_fixed.why: Deliberate, and the substance is unchanged. The mark pins say 'names Aurelian Skin and carries its brand mark, recovered as artwork from the photographed carton' rather than 'identifies Aurelian Skin with its brand mark'. That keeps the existing checks that require the name (range-launch H001, retailer-carousel-p01 H001/H002) grounded, since the carton mark itself reads only AURELIAN around an A monogram (asset_plan prompt for aurelian_carton_front.jpg). The face check says 'type set on ... apart from the recovered mark and the photographed product labels', which is tighter than the suggested 'every line of type'.

not_fixed.problem: Evidence lines framed 'Truth constraint:' and 'Brand assets status:' condense their TASK_SPEC source (for example 'preserve product geometry; retouching may not change what the subject is').
not_fixed.why: Left as is. GUIDE rule 9's verbatim requirement is for quotes from supplied files. These are TASK_SPEC fields, and the condensed wording keeps the meaning (checked against truth_constraints[3] and brand_assets_status). Neither reviewer flagged them. The one misquote that added words ('missing or weak') was fixed.

not_fixed.problem: Reviewer 2 (COVERAGE, NAMING AND FORM), inside its source_record fix, said 'Keep the four source_image bindings as they are.'
not_fixed.why: Reviewer 1 gave a concrete reason to drop them, and the files bear it out. photographer_notes.txt lists shot 1 'Entry, exterior front', but that frame is room_12.jpg (asset_plan prompt 'front entry'), and the living room, shot 3, is room_01.jpg. asset_plan.json says photographer_notes.txt exists to 'help identify which frame is which room', and the register binding would hand that mapping to the executor. GUIDE rule 2 says 'When in doubt, do not bind', and PHOTO-04 binds nothing. The brief pins and the file-named checks keep every deliverable unambiguous for graders, so the bindings were dropped. Reviewer 2 offered no argument for keeping them.

not_fixed.problem: Reviewer 1 proposed a single K1_Q5 house-number check that passes if the '27' is 'cropped out or disclosed'.
not_fixed.why: I split it into two one-fact checks (GUIDE rule 9): '27' not legible, and no number painted in or altered. I did not accept disclosure as a pass, because a grader scoring portal-hero.png cannot see the delivery manifest. A hero for 14 Ridgeway Lane that shows a legible '27' misidentifies the property, and cropping the number out is easy because the door and path lie left of it (about x 3700 of 6000). Retouching the number out is not penalised by the geometry check, which covers roofline, glazing, door and path.

not_fixed.problem: Reviewer 2 noted that the 5% accent cap in palette_rules.distribution is not in the accent checks.
not_fixed.why: I rewrote the accent checks exactly as the reviewer's fix asked (Bay Grey as hairline rules or dividers only; Sage and Stone as small accents; never a ground, panel or type colour). The 5% area cap stays only in palette_rules, as in the PHOTO-04 reference, because a Yes/No grader cannot measure 5% of the designed area reliably.

not_fixed.problem: Reviewer 1 suggested rewriting portal H002 to cover wording and added image elements in one check.
not_fixed.why: The problem is covered, in a different form: I kept H002 as the single wording check and added a separate check on halcyon_canal.jpg for the visual side (reviewer 2's option). That avoids a check testing two facts. I did not add this visual check to the hoarding or poster. The acceptance line "does not imply completed construction" belongs only to the portal. The poster pictures a show apartment, which is finished and furnished by design, and its fidelity check already covers additions. On the hoarding, "planting" would wrongly catch benign pavement shrubs in the area widened out from halcyon_elevation_a.jpg; the existing widening and H002 checks cover it.

not_fixed.problem: Reviewer 2 suggested replacing the poster Spindle check (K1_Q5, "$940,000, not the 895,000 printed on the card") by relying on the new check for old card figures.
not_fixed.why: Not a defect, so I left it as it was. The Spindle check tests something the new check does not: that the Spindle is actually offered at the CSV price. The new check tests that no old card figure appears anywhere, including the $3,780 monthly figure. They overlap on one clause and are not duplicates, and the validator's duplicate guard passed.

not_fixed.problem: Issue 12, part 1: add a separate K2_Q3 check on restoration-06 and share-06 saying '... reads no more orange than hollis_scan_06.jpg; its fade is not warmed further to blend with the set.'

Gone very orange." Part 2 of issue 12 (the sepia, Linen or Paper White wash check on every sampled output) was added.

not_fixed.problem: Items 5 and 15 proposed keeping an Ash Grey fine-print exception in the type-colour check ('except small fine print in Ash Grey #5A5A5C or a small label in Subdued Brass #9C8459').

not_fixed.problem: Item 2 offered an alternative: take the house-mark clause out of traps_preserved and log the trap as untested.
not_fixed.why: The primary fix was chosen instead: pin the placement and add the checks. asset_plan.json marks ostra_house_mark_plate.jpg as defect_engineered with role logo_text, and says the mark reproduces 'at the top of the near-black site'. GUIDE rule 1 says never remove engineered difficulty. The one extension beyond the reviewer's text is a matching pin on the reservation story's 'The restaurant name is readable at mobile size.' not_fixed.problem: Coverage review item 12, second half: add 'No ground or panel on <output> is Charcoal #2E2E2C' to all 12 outputs, evidenced by the Charcoal usage 'Never a ground or panel'.
not_fixed.why: Not real once the grounding review's palette item (invented prohibitions) is applied, and the two conflict. No brand file forbids Charcoal as a ground or panel. not_fixed.problem: The alternative fix offered in the production-mark item: drop the #FFFFFF ban and the leaf and colour requirements so the supplied production marks pass.
not_fixed.why: Not taken, because the files contradict the brand identity. The signature move requires 'the olive leaf locked at cap height one leaf width to its left'. The production files have no leaf and carry a traced photograph strip (measured from benchmark_v4/assets/PHOTO-10/*.png: x 62 to 145, ten letter runs and nothing else). not_fixed.problem: The last reviewer item was truncated at 'checks_add, compound checks on all 12 ou...', so its exact list of checks and its proposed fix are unknown.

not_fixed.problem: Item 5 (partly): A006 on shade-card-r007 ('Mulberry') was said to be a blocking conflict with the Mulberry Dusk drift check, and A008 on shade-card-r006 ('24') a blocking conflict with $24.
not_fixed.why: Neither blocks. verify_outputs.py (benchmark_v4) implements pdf_text_contains as `expected in actual` after whitespace-only normalisation. 'Mulberry' is a substring of 'Mulberry Dusk', and '24' is a substring of '$24', so a correct card passes both. not_fixed.problem: Item 19 (partly): restrict the bottle source on the feed, comparison, product page and story to the three V4 files only.

not_fixed.problem: Item 8 (partly): the feed ad also leaves open which shade its bottle shows.

not_fixed.problem: Item 15 wording: 'remove "with no capital letter" from the seven card checks'.
not_fixed.why: Removing only those words leaves 'set all in lowercase', which still fails alongside the case-sensitive A006. The card check was replaced with the exact rule text instead ('not set in all capitals'), which passes alongside A006, and the lowercase blocker is logged for the automatic-check owner. The four designs keep the full lowercase check.

not_fixed.problem: Issues 1 and 9, preferred route: stop the register from certifying the swapped lines, either by removing provenance_line from source_record on all ten details or by rewording record_field_policy on them.
not_fixed.why: Both are outside what this patch may do. GUIDE rule 2 says to leave existing bindings alone. apply_feedback.py applies sentence edits only to the brief, the group requirements, required_content and acceptance_requirements, so it never reaches record_field_policy. Its guard also rejects a source_record whose values differ from raw_values, so removing the field from values only would be refused. Both reviewers called this an orchestrator-level change and said to escalate. I used their stated fallback, recorded the leftover conflict in traps_preserved[0], and added an ESCALATION entry to change_log. That entry proposes treating all ten details identically, so rows 3 and 5 are not singled out, and says never to print the corrected lines in the register. If the orchestrator makes that change, the pin can require the provenance line again and the two K1_Q5 checks can drop 'Any'.

not_fixed.problem: Finding 7's suggested wording limited the only panel to 'one plain white #FFFFFF frame behind the photograph'.
not_fixed.why: I did not use that wording because it would have written the finding-2 contradiction into every plate. datasheet_2025_PRINT.pdf draws three #FFFFFF panels keyed in #2B2F33: the photo frame at 499,53, the drawing frame at 53,333, and the pricing panel at 348,333, which carries the #E8A31D rule. The panel check was still added on all 12 plates, worded to the corrected rule.

not_fixed.problem: Finding 12 asked for a check that the part number is set at 72 px and the spec lines at 22 px.
not_fixed.why: I added only the measurable part, the 34 px spec-line spacing, and recorded the rest in change_log (the reviewer's second option). Reading a rendered font size off a PNG needs font metrics such as IBM Plex Mono's cap height or advance width. No supplied file gives them, and GUIDE rule 9 forbids values typed from memory. The relative sizes stay covered by the existing hierarchy check on every plate.

not_fixed.problem: Minor: equipment-pdp-r007 has no knockout check. The reviewer proposed 'Wherever the ground shows through the Winch Line Damper ..., such as its grommets, it is the module's own ground, with no grey sweep from summit_bench_packshots_06.jpg left behind.'
not_fixed.why: Not real, and the proposed check would fail a correct output. asset_plan.json marks summit_bench_packshots_06.jpg as 'clean solid SKU (winch line damper)', a folded blanket, with no see-through defect. I located all four grommets in the frame and sampled their hole centres (at 1000 px width): RGB (26,26,26), (32,31,31), (10,10,10) and (71,71,70). The pale sweep measures (218,219,224) to (228,231,235). So every grommet shows the dark Cordura of the fold underneath, not the sweep. A faithful cut-out keeps that fabric inside the grommets, so a check requiring the module ground to show through them would be wrong. I kept summit_bench_packshots_06.jpg in NO_OPENING, where the builder already excludes it on purpose.

not_fixed.problem: Issues 2 and 4, preferred fix: repair frames 01, 05, 06, 07, 11, 12 and 14 with a masked inpaint so the labels agree with slabvault_lots.csv.
not_fixed.why: A patch cannot change assets. GUIDE.md says 'You do not edit corpus files' and the patch schema has no field for assets. Each asset's sha256, S3 key and public URL live in TASK_SPEC.json under docs/gatsby-v5, which I may not edit, so a repaired image would leave those stale. I used the reviewers' fallback, recording the conflicts as traps and checking them, and wrote in traps_preserved item 4 that the lasting fix is a masked inpaint plus new hashes. That repair still needs to be done as a separate asset-repair step.

not_fixed.problem: Issue 4, fallback fix: remove 'from that lot's row in slabvault_lots.csv' from the pin for the certification number.
not_fixed.why: Not done, because it would bring back an unpinned choice that the existing checks already settle. The H007 checks on all 28 tiles, which this patch does not change, already score the CSV value. Example: 'The certification number on ... (listing-front-r002.png) reads exactly "GX-3391045", as approved in slabvault_lots.csv, row 2.' Each deliverable's record_field_policy also says 'The approved_values in source_record are the scoring target', and those values equal the CSV. The house note says the number goes 'on the ticket exactly as printed on the holder label'. The ticket is the printed sleeve ticket (slabvault_lot_card.pdf), which is not one of the 28 PNG outputs. Most frames print no readable number (02, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11, 12 and 13), so 'as printed on the label' cannot be the rule for tiles. I made the conflict visible instead: traps_preserved item 5, the change_log, and 8 checks requiring the delivery manifest to record the mismatch.

not_fixed.problem: Issue 14: make front-r010/H002 conditional ('If ... carries a photograph, at 100% zoom it still shows every condition detail visible in slabvault_consignment_2026F_09.jpg').
not_fixed.why: Not done because it conflicts with issue 3, which is real and fixed. Frame 09 is the back of a different item's slab, labelled 2023 BASEBALL ROOKIE CARD #101 GEM MT 10. Any check that measures the LOT-009 tile against frame 09's condition assumes that frame is LOT-009's photograph. H002 was therefore rewritten into the K1_Q5 'does not present slabvault_consignment_2026F_09.jpg ... as LOT-009' check, as issue 3 proposed.

not_fixed.problem: Issue 11 on listing-detail-r010 only: add a conditional 100% zoom condition check against slabvault_consignment_2026F_09.jpg.
not_fixed.why: Same reason as issue 14. Frame 09 is not a photograph of LOT-009, so its condition details are not LOT-009's. Detail-r010 instead has the 'not presented as LOT-009', 'no comic front shown', 'no frame from another lot' and reshoot-flag checks. The check was added to the other 13 detail tiles.

not_fixed.problem: Issue 8's suggested wording, which asks the crest to draw 'its gold parts, such as the outer ring and chevron bars' in Cup Gold, citing the 2025 PDF's 'outer ring and two chevron bars'.
not_fixed.why: That wording would contradict the crest-match check, r002 H007 and its copies, which match the crest to cup26_sleeve_patch.jpg. On the patch, all three chevron bars and the inner ring are silver thread; the outer ring border, the lettering, the stars and 2026 are gold. On cup26_card_2025_PRINTER.pdf the vector curves give outer ring #C9A233, inner ring #C7CCD1, and chevron bars gold, silver, gold. The two sources agree only on a gold outer ring. The added check therefore requires Cup Gold on the outer ring and not on the chevrons. The problem itself (no check that Cup Gold appears in the crest) is fixed.

not_fixed.problem: Issue 9's suggested wording: 'Floodlit Black #0B0E14 is the dominant ground on <card>, solid around and behind the player photograph in the upper part of the card.'
not_fixed.why: In cup26_card_2025_PRINTER.pdf the photograph fills the full width of the upper 62% (55.1 mm of 88.9 mm), and the ground's fade starts at 58%. So the only ground that shows on the brand's own card is the fade below the photo. Requiring visible dominance, or solid black around the photo, would fail the reference card. Requiring solid black directly under the photo would contradict r004 H004 ('card field is Pitch Deep Navy'). I added a presence-and-order check instead: Floodlit Black shows as ground, above the navy card field. The mandatory colour is now checked on every card, and nothing contradicts the 2025 card or H004.

not_fixed.problem: Issue 1 asks for a pass value of 'tracked +15 units', and issue 12 asks the same for the surname's +20 units.
not_fixed.why: Issue 12 (same review set) says these unit values are not reliably visible. At 5 pt, +15/1000 em is about 0.075 pt. So the pass condition is 'slightly open letterspacing, not tight or negative tracking', and the exact unit value from type_system is quoted in the evidence. The limit is still checked on every card, in a form a grader can judge.

not_fixed.problem: Reviewer 2 asked to replace all 16 one-gallery checks with one template ending 'the uplighting colour on the walls of hartley_select_NN.jpg is not judged'. Reviewer 1 asked for a different wording on the reception frames only.
not_fixed.why: Both findings are real and are fixed together, but not word for word. Frames 01-10 are lit by window light or sun, not uplighting, so the uplighting clause is used only where BLOCK is amber or magenta (asset_plan defect_engineered). Review-10 does not get the skin form: the couple fill about 60x170 px of the 1600 px frame, and reviewer 1's own finding says skin there is too small to judge. It compares its garden greens with the other golden-hour review images instead.

not_fixed.problem: The K5_Q2 finding asked to keep review-02/H003 and review-03/H004 at K5_Q1 and add a new K5_Q2 check to all 22 outputs, worded 'keep the same brightness relative to the background'.
not_fixed.why: The result is the same as asked: 22 K5_Q1 and 22 K5_Q2 checks, one of each per output. The route differs. The two existing checks keep their original K5_Q2 tag (origin k_gap_fill), because review-03/H004 was already a faces-against-background check. The first-read K5_Q1 checks for 02 and 03 are added as new checks instead. I also wrote the check as 'no darker than in the source' rather than 'the same brightness'. The second-shooter frames 04 and 09 have to gain contrast to match their block, and a same-brightness check on them is the 'no shift at all' pattern that GUIDE section 9 warns against.

not_fixed.problem: Findings 3 and 18: the reviewers proposed different single-sentence rewrites of the combined-run layout check.
not_fixed.why: Both concerns are real and both are fixed, but not with either sentence verbatim. Reviewer A's sentence comes to 44 words, over the 40-word limit in GUIDE rule 9, and bundles two facts. Reviewer B's sentence would exempt page 6 from any layout consistency. I split it into two checks: the monogram, name and text block consistent on all 8 pages, and the portrait frame consistent on every page that carries a portrait.

not_fixed.problem: Finding 11: the proposed fix was to append ', set together as one block with nothing covering or blocking it' to H002.
not_fixed.why: Appending would make H002 42 words, over the 40-word limit, and give it two facts. The requirement is restored as its own K1_Q1 check on the one-pager instead.

not_fixed.problem: Reviewer B, item 13: add a separate brief_insertion after 'Use the supplied approved copy and factual records.' to settle the caption deck, and a separate Regular-weight check on p01 to p06 (item 11).
not_fixed.why: Both problems are real and both are fixed, just in a different form. A second insertion on that anchor would be placed ahead of the existing price insertion, because insert_brief inserts right after the anchor, so the brief would be scrambled. The caption face is pinned in the caption sentence edit instead, which also updates the group requirements and every carousel page's required_content and acceptance_requirements. The Regular weight was folded into the carousel post caption and body face check instead of a seventh typography check per page. That matches the feature's existing body check, which pairs face and weight, and it avoids grading the same caption twice for face.

not_fixed.problem: Reviewer B, item 22, alternative: add a K2_Q3 check on each output that Kiln Clay, Ember and Sprig Green together cover no more than 5% of the designed area.
not_fixed.why: The reviewer offered this as one of two options. I took the other one: the 5% clause was removed from the check's evidence, so no check now cites a cap it does not grade. An area percentage is hard for a grader to judge objectively. The role checks already fail any accent used as a ground, panel, headline or caption. If you prefer the PHOTO-02/PHOTO-13 approach (forbid off-palette card inks), all light type would have to move to Laser Cyan or Concrete, and several checks would need rewording.

EVENT LINE READING: the type system's step 01 (sample PULSEVAULT, 'the cover event line') makes the cover event line the brand name set in Didot, next to the painted mark. The pin says 'our name in Didot' so that this can coexist with the rule 'never re-typeset the painted wall mark'. Worth a human look.

SCREEN OVER PHOTOS: the card darkens its floor still with a Blackout gradient (rasterised in the PDF, so no exact percentage can be read from the asset). The opacity rule allows a Blackout-only screen over a picture and forbids everything else. The card's soft black text shadow is neither required nor forbidden.
readiness.blockers still says 'Supply a cleared music track', although pulsevault_bed.wav (20 s) is supplied. This is outside the patch schema.

The example banned words in the voice checks (unforgettable, immersive, curated, world-class) are illustrations in the style of the PHOTO-04 reference, not quoted brand facts. The underlying rule is quoted verbatim from pulsevault_next_date.txt.

pins: Poster brief sentence: the poster bills all four acts in the lineup's row order and every date is accurate; the first row (the next show) is the headline with its picture, billing line, date, door time and ticket price; each later act follows with its own date and ticket price; the moth and lamp mark appears at least once. Poster group requirement, required content and acceptance line 'The billing order matches the lineup.' were rewritten to the same content as the brief pin, so the brief and every copy stay in sync.

Poster 'The show date is accurate.' now reads: every date and ticket price on the poster is its own act's, exactly as the lineup file gives it. Poster acceptance 'The show date matches the approved source exactly.' now reads: every date matches its act's row of the lineup file.
Square 'next-show action' (group requirement and acceptance) now reads 'the next-show date line, Friday, October 17, 2026'. The square's required content asks for nothing else in words.

Film 'The act is identified accurately.' now reads 'the act on the end card, next month's act'. Film 'act identifier matches the approved source' now reads 'the act name on the end card matches the lineup file exactly'. traps: Attribution: the six takes show this month's singer, who is named in no source. Junie Ash must be billed as Next and never given the footage. The brief settles this, so it was not pinned further. It is now checked on both films (never over a shot of the filmed singer).
Off-axis framing: the singer is left of centre with the stool and black road cases beside her. The square crop is left for the executor to check.

Coverage: all six takes (velvet_hour_set_take.mp4, velvet_hour_take_02.mp4 to velvet_hour_take_06.mp4) are about 5 s long and silent, measured with ffprobe and matching motion_source_metadata.json. Act photographs on neutral filenames, left as supplied: next_month_act_01.jpg (cold studio grade, tight crop), next_month_act_02.jpg (cool overcast wide group), next_month_act_03.jpg (675 x 900 phone screengrab), next_month_act_04.jpg (photographed press sheet with a halftone that blooms into moire). The pin says 'its picture', never a filename. Conditional checks cover pixelation on 03 and moire on 04 if either is used.

The lamp-box mark in velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg is untouched and now checked on the poster: the hairline arc of small caps type that drops out when the whole mark is named, the enclosed wing counters that knock out to a filled slab, cream running close to the green in the shaded right third, and paint thickest at the wing edges so the counters close at poster size.

The bar stills velvet_hour_still_01.jpg to velvet_hour_still_11.jpg are untouched: heavy warm cast and grain, the 07/08 twin pair (07 softer with eyes open, 08 sharper with eyes closed), and the empty-stool red herring in 11.

velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf is untouched: a single continuous text story whose static tagline kicker a mapping readout drops, and no bleed box. It is read only as the brand's colour hierarchy.
No source_record was added. The lineup's billing lines, dates and prices are printed nowhere in the output register.
concerns: Duplicate check ids in the corpus: MOTION-18/show-poster/H001 and H002 each appear twice in VERIFIERS.json and TASK_SPEC. The apply tool rewrites only the later copy. My modifies keep the later copies' meaning (H001: the named billing order; H002: the lamp-box mark, now its three parts). H007 was refocused on 'rebuilt as flat artwork' so it no longer repeats H002. The earlier copies ('billed in the same order as the lineup' and 'the show date matches velvet_hour_lineup.csv exactly') stay as they are, still under the brand-prefixed name 'Velvet Hour / Next-show poster'. The tool's ATOMIC_VERIFIERS_ALL100.json merge also collapses both copies of each id into the later one. Fixing this needs the ids renumbered across the corpus, which the patch schema cannot do.

Stale per-task register: tasks/MOTION-18/OUTPUT_REGISTER.json and DELIVERABLES.md still say the film is 1920x1080 16:9, 20 to 30 s, and the story cut is 1080x1920 9:16, 12 to 15 s. TASK_SPEC, the brief and OUTPUT_REGISTER_ALL100.json all say 1080x1920 at 12 to 15 s and a 1080x1080 square at 6 to 10 s. The brief tells the executor the register defines sizes, so the two contradict each other. The patch is not allowed to change specs, so this was not fixed here.
The brief says permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence, but MOTION-18 supplies no owner note file. The line was left as it is.

motion_source_metadata.json lists only velvet_hour_set_take.mp4. Takes 02 to 06 and the bed are marked s3_upload_pending in TASK_SPEC assets, so reference URLs in the new take and bed checks may not resolve until they are uploaded. The readiness blocker still says one silent 5 s clip is insufficient even though five more takes are now supplied. asset_plan's narrative for the set take (a 47-minute 1920x1080 take with host speech) does not match the supplied file. This is harmless because the measured metadata is authoritative.

Two band names (The Paper Kestrels, Cinder and Salt) have no given name and surname. The stack rule is checked as 'two lines, second line in true small caps', and no split is pinned. The given-name-above-surname check names only Junie Ash and Odette Vann.
Not checked because a grader could not see it: step 01 and 02 tracking of minus 5 or minus 3 units on the given name. 'Short sentences' has no length, so the 65-character measure stands in for it.

The mandatory Back Room Green check on the square means the square needs some designed green element, such as a panel or closing card. This follows from the palette rules grounded in the listing card.

pins: Scenario number, pinned by a criterion: 'that scenario's place in the running order of the approved copy' (brief insertion). The required content now says Right turns 2, Four-way stops 7 and Lane changes 1. The type system requires a number on every scenario, but no source said which number, and the output ids r003 and r008 suggest 3 and 8. The 2019 guide footer ('3 / 8' on the Left turns across traffic page) numbers pages the same way as the running order.

Upright example: the brief sentence 'The scenario title and the callout only' now reads 'The scenario number, the scenario title and the callout only, with no steps'. The type system's signature move gives the vertical cutdown a number, and the brief did not.

Stop glyph placement: the Four-way stops explainer shows 'our simplified stop sign shape, recovered from the wall sheet' at least once, and its required content names the STOP octagon from milepost_glyph_sheet.jpg. H006 checked the glyph, but no requirement put it on any film. Only its placement is pinned; how it is recovered is still the test.

Stale narration requirements restated from the brief: 'The narration matches the visual scenario.' (group and both explainers), 'The complete spoken instruction is audible without missing words.' and 'The complete instruction is intelligible.' (upright example). Each contradicted the brief's No narration and silent clips.
The upright example's acceptance line 'The road-context area shown in the supplied source...' now names the lane line, as the brief does.
traps: The brief says the four-way stop takes are one junction filmed on two passes. That stays as the test: a check fails any title, caption or cut that presents them as two junctions. Which of takes 07, 08, 13 and 14 to use is not pinned.

Every take measures 5.042 s with no audio (motion_source_metadata.json plus ffprobe of takes 09 to 16), and these measurements override asset_plan's long narrated takes. A 12 to 15 s or 10 to 12 s film needs several distinct takes. Looping stays a failure, and no take order is pinned.

The brief's rule stands: any step the footage cannot show is named in the delivery manifest, never faked with unrelated road shots. The existing visible-manoeuvre checks are kept, and each film also gets a manifest check.

milepost_glyph_sheet.jpg is still a phone photo of a taped wall sheet: the glyph must be lifted from the ink, not the paper, tape or tiles, and a new check tests this. The shadowed corner and the enclosed yield outline are untouched.
milepost_county_sign.jpg's knockout-bite defect is untouched and bound nowhere. The stale check that demanded the sign in the four-way stop film was rewritten.

The road stills keep their defects (clipped skies on 01 and 02, windscreen reflection and polariser band on 03 and 04, the lean on 05). The existing source_image bindings (still_03 and still_01) and source_record bindings are left alone.
milepost_copy_2026.csv keeps its uneven step lists (3 to 11 lines) and the Roundabouts row's Photo, milepost_roundabout_ref.jpg, which does not exist. Neither row is commissioned here.
milepost_guide_2019.pdf keeps its italic serif callout, bold grotesque title, fixed steps frame and missing bleed. The type system overrides them, and checks now test the type system.
concerns: No file labels the scenes of takes 09 to 16; the metadata covers only 01 to 08. I identified them by watching contact strips: 02 and 09 to 12 are the right-turn junction and street, 07, 13 and 14 are the four-way stop from the cockpit, and 01, 15 and 16 are the upright lane-change road. The asset-selection checks name these files, and the evidence says the scenes were read by watching.

In the contact strips, none of takes 02 or 09 to 12 clearly shows the car completing a right turn; they appear to cross or continue straight. The existing check r003/H003 (visibly completes a right turn) may be unpassable. TASK_SPEC readiness already carries a blocker that the short silent takes cannot show the full instructions.
Visually, take_08 (a green-roof corner store, no mountains) does not look like the same junction as takes 07, 13 and 14. The brief asserts it is the same junction, so this was left as client-settled.
In a small thumbnail, a stop sign in take_13 looked misspelled; I did not confirm this at full resolution and wrote no check for it.

Other per-task files are stale and outside this patch: OUTPUT_REGISTER.json and DELIVERABLES.md still list 9 outputs with speech and 20 to 35 s durations, and the readiness blocker still asks for narration. The apply tool rewrites only their required_content and acceptance lines.

pins: Brief item 1: the Cobbleway campaign film shows the name and price of Wildflower Granola (foldgrain_service_copy.txt marks it '(the hero of the range)'), copied exactly, plus the FOLD & GRAIN wordmark. The required content already asked for this.

Brief item 2: the Cobbleway vertical cutdown shows Wildflower Granola's name and price, and every carton in shot stays whole from top to bottom. The required content changes 'The carton held whole' to 'Every carton in shot held whole, top to bottom'.

Brief items 3 and 4 and the Lunara film and cutdown required content: the on-screen piece changes from Ridge Pendant to Thread Pendant, which has the same $180 price. asset_plan.json says Ridge Pendant has no usable grab, so featuring it went against the brief's own instruction to name such a piece as not deliverable. The brief never names Ridge or Halo.

Brief items 5 and 6, the board group requirement, required content and acceptance line: 'the actual final campaign frames' now means each cell is built from one of the supplied frame grabs of the product it shows, with nothing generated. The films are continuous passes with no product named on screen, so they cannot give each product its own cell.

Brief, Lunara softbox paragraph: a piece with no usable frame keeps its own board cell with its name over its price, and the cell says it is not deliverable from this take. This uses the copy sheet's own wording and does not say which pieces are affected.

Brief item 7, plus the service group requirement, required content and acceptance line: every line of the service-page section of foldgrain_service_copy.txt must appear word for word (headings in Engravers capitals), and each client example shows only its own client's work.
traps: The lens-capped tail of cobbleway_take_4k.mov stays in the brief as written and its check is kept. A new check covers the hand and camera-rig frames that actually end the file.

The warm and cool split across the Cobbleway Provisions grabs is not named in the brief or palette rules. 12 of the 24 grabs are cool. All grabs of Smoky Tomato Soup (cobbleway_grab_17 to 20) and Maple Oat Bars (cobbleway_grab_21 to 24) are cool. Only the checks name these files.
The executor still has to decide which Lunara Silver pieces have no usable frame. The brief pins where such a piece is named but never names Ridge Pendant or Halo Pendant.

The usable grab still varies from piece to piece in the Lunara set and cannot be predicted from file order. Checks fail only grabs that visibly cut the pendant at the frame edge (lunara_grab_03, 08, 15, 20, 23) or are motion-soft (lunara_grab_09, 21).

The price band is written '$2,200 - $3,500' in the copy but '$2,200 to $3,500' in the type-system sample. The copy's NOTES (prices exactly as written) settle this, and H002 still requires the copy's form.
The Cobbleway walk-through audio is unusable and nothing may be scripted or synthesised in its place. The only allowed sound is cobbleway_bed.wav.

Both client marks are untouched and the brief still places them nowhere: cobbleway_carton_face.jpg closes its counters at caption size, and lunara_bail_stamp.jpg is a punched stamp with no ink. Conditional checks catch a closed-counter mark or a blob wherever one is used.
The portrait lunara_take_4k.mov pass and the grey-card claims are untouched.
Wildflower Granola is named because the copy file marks it as the hero. Its price is still a lookup in the copy.
concerns: Judgement call to review: swapping the Lunara films from Ridge Pendant to Thread Pendant. It keeps the $180 price and hides the trap, but it does change the featured piece that TASK_SPEC set. The edit is sentence_edits[2], [3], [4] and [5] plus the modified check client-film-lunara/H001.

A planned defect is not visible in the pixels. At 1:1, lunara_grab_04 to 06 (Ridge Pendant) and lunara_grab_16 to 18 (Halo Pendant) show no faces clipped to flat white. The grabs the plan labels 'clipped' (01, 10, 13, 22, 25) do not have more flat white than its 'usable' grabs; grab_19 has the largest flat patch. So no check fails a Ridge or Halo frame by filename. The boards are graded on the brief's own test instead: a whole, sharp frame with detail in the brightest face, or a cell that says the piece is not deliverable. The Ridge and Halo trap needs the assets regenerated before it can work.

cobbleway_take_4k.mov is 5.04 s and 1920x1088 and does not end on black: from about 4.2 s a hand and a camera rig enter the frame. There is no grey card at the start of either pass. So the brief's lens-cap statement does not match the file.

The footage does not match the grabs. The Lunara passes show ten pendants in two rows on a slab, not the nine grab pieces. The Cobbleway passes show unlabelled kraft cartons marked '183'. Film fidelity checks therefore compare against the clips, and the existing tall-lunara/H001, which compared against the grabs and would have failed an honest cut, was rewritten. lunara_take_4k.mov and lunara_take_04.mp4 also show the strip softbox fixture in frame. That is not graded, because the brief has no rule on it.

Stale files the apply tool does not fix. The per-task OUTPUT_REGISTER.json and DELIVERABLES.md still say the films run 20 to 30 s and the talls 12 to 15 s, and give the Lunara films music audio. The brief and TASK_SPEC say 10 to 12 s, 6 to 8 s and silent. The brief tells the executor to rely on 'the output register', and RELEASE_GATES.json and readiness blockers still say no Lunara footage or music was supplied.

The palette's per-client grounds (Paper White for Cobbleway, Ink Black for Lunara) and Kraft Tan limited to Cobbleway material come from the brief's identity split and the measured grounds of the footage and grabs, not from any supplied brand file. No studio card or sheet exists in the pack to check them against.
